title: Goldman Sachs Finds Workers Displaced by AI Transition Into Other At-Risk Roles
summary:
Workers who lose their jobs to artificial intelligence typically remain unemployed for longer periods before finding new roles that are also susceptible to automation, an analysis by Goldman Sachs found. The bank's research indicates that displaced employees often transition into other positions that AI is likely to replace, creating a cycle of repeated job instability.

The findings expand on previous Goldman projections that a 15% increase in productivity driven by AI could displace about 9% of the global workforce, including roughly 15 million workers in the US. The bank also noted that the negative impact of AI is spreading to nonmanufacturing industries, where higher adoption is now linked to higher unemployment rates and slower employment growth.
